services.name: Mobile Brake Repair
services.blurb: Pads, rotors, calipers, and hardware replaced in your driveway. We measure pad thickness and rotor runout on site, show you the numbers, then price the job before anything comes apart.
symptoms: Squealing or grinding when you slow down
Steering wheel or pedal shudder under braking
Brake warning light or low pedal
Visible scoring on the rotor face
included: Four-wheel pad and rotor measurement
Caliper slide and piston inspection
Brake fluid condition check
Torque-to-spec reinstall and road test

faqs.q: Can brakes really be done in a driveway?
faqs.a: Yes. Brake service is the single most common mobile job we run. Our vans carry jack stands, torque wrenches, a rotor kit, and a full pad inventory for the most common makes, so most brake jobs finish in one visit without your car ever leaving the house.

faqs.q: Do I need rotors or just pads?
faqs.a: We measure before we quote. If the rotor is above the manufacturer's minimum thickness and running true, pads alone are fine and you pay less. If it is under spec or warped, replacing it is the only safe call and we will show you the measurement.

faqs.q: Is the brake job warrantied?
faqs.a: Yes - 12 months or 12,000 miles on parts and labor, whichever comes first. If a pad or rotor we installed fails in that window, we come back out and make it right at no charge.

services.name: Check Engine Light Diagnostic
services.priceUnit: diagnostic hold, applied to the repair
services.blurb: A real diagnosis, not a parts-store code read. We pull live data, run the manufacturer test procedure for the stored code, and tell you what actually failed and what it costs to fix.
symptoms: Check engine or service engine soon light
Rough idle, misfire, or hesitation
Failed state inspection on emissions
Sudden drop in fuel economy
included: Full OBD-II scan with freeze-frame data
Live sensor data under load
Manufacturer test procedure for the stored code
Written findings plus a priced repair plan

faqs.q: Why pay for a scan when a parts store does it free?
faqs.a: A free scan reads the code and stops there. A P0171 code, for example, can be a vacuum leak, a failing mass airflow sensor, a weak fuel pump, or an exhaust leak upstream of the sensor. We run the test that separates them, so you replace the part that actually failed instead of guessing.

faqs.q: What happens to the $100 hold?
faqs.a: It is a hold, not a separate fee. If you approve the repair with us, the full $100 is credited against the job. You only lose it if you decline the work entirely.

faqs.q: Can you clear the code so I can pass inspection?
faqs.a: We can clear it, but clearing a code without fixing the cause resets the emissions readiness monitors and you will fail inspection anyway until the drive cycle completes. We would rather fix the fault and clear it properly.

services.name: Mobile Battery Replacement
services.blurb: We come to the dead car. Load test first, because a battery that fails to crank is sometimes a charging system problem, then swap it, register it if your vehicle needs it, and clean the terminals.
symptoms: Slow crank or a click when you turn the key
Dash lights dim when cranking
Battery or charging warning light
Needing a jump more than once
included: Load test on the existing battery
Alternator output and parasitic draw check
Battery registration on vehicles that require it
Terminal and cable cleaning, old battery recycled

faqs.q: My car will not start at all. Can you still come?
faqs.a: That is exactly the job. The car does not need to run for us to work on it - we bring power, tools, and the replacement battery to wherever it is parked.

faqs.q: Is it the battery or the alternator?
faqs.a: We test both before selling you anything. A battery that keeps dying is often a failing alternator or a parasitic draw, and replacing the battery alone would leave you stranded again in a few weeks.

faqs.q: Do newer cars need the battery registered?
faqs.a: Many do. Most BMW, Mercedes, Audi, VW, and a growing number of domestic vehicles run a charging strategy tied to battery age. We register the new battery to the vehicle so the charging system treats it correctly.

services.name: Starter & Alternator Replacement
services.blurb: Charging and starting system work done on site. We confirm the failure with a voltage drop and output test before we sell a part, then replace it with the car where it sits.
symptoms: Battery light on while driving
Headlights dimming at idle
Single loud click, no crank
Whining or grinding when starting
included: Charging system output test under load
Voltage drop test on the starter circuit
Belt and tensioner inspection
Post-install output verification

faqs.q: Is this really a driveway job?
faqs.a: On most vehicles, yes. Some transverse V6 layouts bury the starter under the intake, and if yours is one of them we will tell you up front and route the job to our Justin shop hub instead of burning your afternoon.

faqs.q: How do you know it is the alternator and not the battery?
faqs.a: An alternator should hold roughly 13.5 to 14.7 volts at the battery with the engine running and a load applied. We test that, plus ripple voltage, which catches a failing diode that a simple voltage check misses.

faqs.q: Do you use remanufactured parts?
faqs.a: We offer both. Remanufactured units cost less and carry a shorter warranty; new units cost more and last longer. We quote both and let you pick - and either way the 12-month/12,000-mile labor warranty applies.

services.name: Mobile Oil Change
services.blurb: Full synthetic oil and a quality filter, done in your driveway while you keep working. No waiting room, no upsell board, and we haul the used oil away for recycling.
symptoms: Oil life monitor at or below 15%
Six months or more since the last change
Dark, gritty oil on the dipstick
Due for a service before a road trip
included: Full synthetic oil to manufacturer spec
New oil filter and drain plug gasket
Multi-point courtesy inspection
Tire pressure set, fluids topped, oil recycled

faqs.q: What does an oil change cost?
faqs.a: Most four and six cylinder vehicles land between $75 and $110 with full synthetic. Larger diesel and performance sumps that take 8+ quarts or a cartridge filter run toward $145. You get the exact number before we start.

faqs.q: Do you check anything else while you are here?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is included. Brakes, belts, filters, tire tread and pressure, and all under-hood fluids get a look. If we find something, you get a photo and a price - never a surprise charge.

faqs.q: Where does the used oil go?
faqs.a: Back in the van and to a licensed recycler. Nothing gets poured out at your house, which matters for anyone on a septic system or near a storm drain.

services.name: Pre-Purchase Inspection
services.blurb: Before you hand over money for a used car, we meet you at the seller and go through it. Scan, lift check, fluid condition, frame and paint depth, road test - with a written report and photos you can negotiate with.
symptoms: Buying private party and cannot verify history
Dealer will not allow a shop inspection
Out-of-state vehicle with unknown rust history
Anything with a rebuilt or salvage title
included: Full OBD-II scan including pending and history codes
Undercarriage, frame rail, and leak inspection
Paint depth readings for hidden bodywork
Road test plus a photo report within the hour

faqs.q: Can you inspect a car at a dealership?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Most independent lots allow it and many franchise dealers will too. We work around what the seller permits - if we cannot get it in the air, the report says so explicitly rather than glossing over it.

faqs.q: How fast do I get the report?
faqs.a: Typically within the hour, while you are still standing there. That is the whole point - a report that lands the next day is useless when someone else is looking at the same car.

faqs.q: Is it worth $145 on a cheap car?
faqs.a: On a $6,000 car it routinely finds $2,000 of deferred work. Either you walk away or you negotiate with a written report in hand. It pays for itself or it confirms you found a good one.

services.name: Lift & Leveling Kit Install
services.blurb: Leveling kits, 2 to 8 inch suspension lifts, coilovers, and the geometry work that has to follow. This is shop work at our Justin hub, not a driveway job, because lift installs require an alignment afterward.
symptoms: Want to clear a larger tire
Factory rake you want to level out
Sagging rear on a work or tow truck
Planning an off-road build
included: Kit fitment review against your tire and wheel plan
Full suspension install to manufacturer torque spec
Driveline angle and brake line clearance check
Post-install alignment coordination

faqs.q: Do you install a kit I bought myself?
faqs.a: Yes. Bring the kit and we will install it. We will also flag fitment problems before we start - the wrong kit for your tire size or a kit missing the hardware to correct driveline angle is a problem worth catching in the parking lot, not halfway through.

faqs.q: Is an alignment required after a lift?
faqs.a: Always. Changing ride height changes camber, caster, and toe. Skipping the alignment will chew through a set of tires in a few thousand miles, so we build it into the plan.

faqs.q: Why is this shop work instead of mobile?
faqs.a: Lift work needs a lift, a press, and alignment equipment. We run it at the Justin hub. Everything else on this site comes to you - this one you bring to us.

services.name: Mobile A/C Repair
services.blurb: Texas summer work. We pressure test, find the actual leak with dye or an electronic sniffer, then evacuate and recharge to the exact factory weight - not a can of stop-leak from a parts store.
symptoms: Air blows cool but never cold
A/C works at highway speed, not at idle
Compressor clutch not engaging
Musty smell or weak airflow at the vents
included: High and low side pressure readings
Electronic leak detection
Evacuate and recharge to factory refrigerant weight
Vent temperature verification before we leave

faqs.q: Can you just top it off?
faqs.a: A system low on refrigerant is leaking - refrigerant does not get used up. We will recharge it, but we find the leak first, because otherwise you are paying us again in six weeks.

faqs.q: Do you handle R-1234yf?
faqs.a: Yes. Most 2015-and-newer vehicles use R-1234yf, which needs different equipment and costs more per pound than R-134a. Our vans are equipped for both.

faqs.q: How cold should the vents actually get?
faqs.a: On a 100-degree North Texas afternoon, a healthy system pulls vent temperature down to roughly 40 to 50 degrees. We measure it before we leave and show you the reading.
